title: 《铁拳8》范马勇次郎亮相
text:
太诡异了.jpg
万代南梦宫首次展示了《铁拳8》DLC角色范马勇次郎。这位来自《刃牙》的角色，造型果然如粉丝预期般诡异。
这款格斗游戏的第3赛季角色新预告在Evo France 2026期间亮相。继州光于6月、鲍勃于8月推出后，由袋鼠母子搭档出战的小罗杰现已正式确定于11月11日开放抢先体验，11月16日正式上线。不过，多数粉丝最期待的那位角色仍未公布确切上线日期。
小罗杰无疑是这段《铁拳8》DLC新预告的主角：预告全长4分钟，其中近3分钟都在展示这位袋鼠拳手的实机玩法。勇次郎的片段则放在末尾，但展示的内容格外令人震惊。下方展示了这位《刃牙》反派来到《铁拳》世界后的全新形象。
勇次郎的表情……至少可以说是相当丰富，因此，如何还原他的面容和隆起的肌肉，注定会引人关注。嗯，万代南梦宫团队已经尽力了。今天的Evo预告只用了几个镜头，展示他标志性的露齿笑容和身体柔韧性。
这位动画联动角色似乎仍在开发中，尚未公布上线日期。不过新预告结尾明确表示，勇次郎的新预告将于2027年1月17日，在铁拳世界巡回赛总决赛期间首播。距离现在还有3个月，因此到时我们或许能看到实机玩法。
回顾此前的日程，万代南梦宫通常会在《铁拳8》两次DLC上线之间留出几个月的间隔。等勇次郎新预告公布时，小罗杰上线也已过去两个月，因此我们也可以期待团队在那段时间公布勇次郎的上线日期。如果运气好，这位《刃牙》角色甚至可能当天就上线。不过，还是要强调，目前他的上线日期尚无任何确切消息。
小罗杰和勇次郎均包含在第3赛季通行证中，两人推出后，该通行证承诺的4名追加角色便将全部到齐。第1和第2赛季的角色包括三岛平八、盔甲豹王、安娜，以及《最终幻想16》主角克莱夫·罗兹菲尔德等。

title: 《生化危机：爆发夜》成为导演扎克·克雷格票房最高的电影
text:
也是评分最高的电子游戏改编电影
《生化危机：爆发夜》超越《凶器》，成为导演扎克·克雷格票房最高的电影。
扎克·克雷格 这部改编自卡普空经典生存恐怖游戏系列的真人电影表现亮眼，截至本周末，全球累计票房预计达到3.202亿美元。其中，北美票房为1.385亿美元，海外票房为1.817亿美元。《生化危机》正式超过《凶器》的2.7亿美元，达到这一成绩所用的时间还少了几周。
克雷格重新构想的浣熊市于2026年9月18日登上大银幕，本周末是影片上映后的第四个周末。中国大陆的首映是本轮票房大幅增长的主要推力，也让影片重返全球周末票房榜首。第四个周末，影片共收获6265万美元，其中仅中国市场就贡献了4060万美元。此前，影片超过《凶器》似乎已无悬念；如今，它不仅登顶克雷格作品票房榜，累计票房也继续远远甩开据报道为7500万美元的制作预算。
《生化危机：爆发夜》首周末便拿下1.083亿美元，由此开启了持续出色的院线表现。这一强劲开局甚至带动了游戏市场，让系列部分游戏销量上涨。克雷格的这部新作也成为有史以来评分最高的电子游戏改编电影。首映前的几个月，网上一直充斥着对这部电影的负面声音。游戏粉丝的讨论大多围绕影片缺少熟悉的角色，以及对背景设定的改动展开。克雷格则辩称，这些改动是为了拍出更好的电影。几乎从各方面来看，这场押注似乎都得到了回报。

title: 《阿特米斯的奇幻历险》获批改编动画
text:
再登荧屏
《阿特米斯的奇幻历险》将以动画剧集的形式重返荧屏，在迪士尼频道和Disney+播出。
在2026年纽约漫展的《阿特米斯的奇幻历险》25周年专题活动上，作家Eoin Colfer宣布，迪士尼已批准另一个改编自他所著合家欢奇幻小说的剧集项目。他也将担任执行制片人，继续参与这部动画剧集。迪士尼承诺，他将「以自己的创作理念，更深入地挖掘这套深受读者喜爱的小说中的角色与世界观；今年恰逢系列首部小说出版25周年」。
与Colfer共同担任执行制片人的，还有漫威动画《月亮女孩与恶魔恐龙》的Ben Juwono，以及《新唐老鸭俱乐部》的Colleen Evanson。这位《阿特米斯的奇幻历险》原作者在声明中表示，他「很自豪，也很高兴能加入这支强大的团队，一起将《阿特米斯的奇幻历险》动画搬上荧屏」。
他补充道：「每个人都才华横溢、积极向上，让我确信精灵世界交给他们再合适不过了。」
《阿特米斯的奇幻历险》动画剧集尚未公布播出日期，但等到它上线时，它并不会是Disney+上首部改编自该系列的作品。2020年，迪士尼推出过一部同名真人电影，但粉丝和影评人大多对它评价不佳。影评汇总网站烂番茄的数据显示，这部直接上线流媒体的电影新鲜度仅为8%，被评为「烂」，观众评分也只有19%。
《阿特米斯的奇幻历险》电影由Ferdia Shaw饰演片名中的主角，Lara McDonnell、Josh Gadd和Michael Rouse也参演了该片。IGN在4分的评测中称其为「一个空洞的科学奇幻故事，角色过目即忘，剧情毫无新意」。换句话说，电影改编的尝试并不成功，而新动画剧集希望能在2020年电影失利的地方取得成功。
剧集简介写道：「动作冒险奇幻剧集《阿特米斯的奇幻历险》围绕13岁的天才少年阿特米斯·法尔展开。他发现了一个地下世界，里面的精灵全副武装、十分危险，而且拥有出人意料的高科技。他展开计划，打算捕捉一只精灵并夺取其魔法，以救治奄奄一息的母亲，拯救自己的家庭。」
《阿特米斯的奇幻历险》首部小说于2001年出版，Colfer在这一世界观下创作的其他故事在全球的总销量超过3500万册。

title: 剧集《银翼杀手2099》预告
text: 在《银翼杀手2049》的故事发生五十年后，洛杉矶迎来了重生，只不过重塑它的人并非人类。为了结束逃亡生涯，孤注一掷的科拉接受了最后一个新身份：银翼杀手。她被迫与时日无多的复制人奥尔温搭档，追捕一名逃跑者，而此人背后藏着的真相，足以让这座摇摇欲坠的城市彻底崩塌。剧集《银翼杀手2099》由乔纳森·范塔勒肯执导，杨紫琼、亨特·莎弗、迪米特里·阿博尔德、刘易斯·格里本等人出演，将于11月25日上线流媒体平台亚马逊Prime Video。

title: 《毁灭战士》作曲家愿意回归系列
text:
「毫不犹豫」
澳大利亚传奇作曲家Mick Gordon曾为2016年的《毁灭战士》及其2020年的续作《毁灭战士：永恒》配乐，让玩家每次爆头都忍不住跟着音乐甩头。他向IGN表示，愿意考虑为id Software这款标志性射击游戏系列的后续作品配乐。在本周末的PAX澳大利亚展会上接受采访时，Gordon似乎暗示，他与《毁灭战士》的合作未必就此结束，尽管《毁灭战士：永恒》发售后，他与开发团队的决裂曾闹得人尽皆知。
Gordon说：「要实现这件事，需要很多块多米诺骨牌以非常特定的方式倒下。如果有一天这些骨牌真能这样倒下，我会回归。当然会。毫不犹豫。」
Gordon没有具体解释这些「多米诺骨牌」可能指什么，但他与《毁灭战士：永恒》执行制作人Marty Stratton之间的纠纷可能尚未彻底解决。2022年，Gordon在Medium发布长文，指控开发商id Software没有支付他为《毁灭战士：永恒》原声音乐所做的一半工作的报酬。他还点名指责Stratton，称自己在制作游戏配乐和原声专辑的整个过程中反复遭到对方辱骂。不过，这段经历看来确实没有削弱Gordon对《毁灭战士》本身的热爱。
Gordon解释道：「关于我想让《毁灭战士》的音乐走向何方，我列过一整份创意清单。我当然希望有朝一日能探索这些想法。」
无论Gordon是否参与，《毁灭战士》的未来会是什么样，则是另一回事。微软持续缩减XBOX业务，许多工作室受到严重冲击，id Software也是其中之一。今年7月，这家《毁灭战士》开发商有136名员工受到裁员影响。当时，服务首席程序员Chris Hays的话被援引报道：「只剩一半的人手，很难做出像我们以前那样的3A游戏。我说很难，其实是指不可能。」
与此同时，Gordon一直忙于多个项目。他为将于10月14日发售的《战锤40K：爆矢枪2》创作了最终Boss战的主题音乐。他也仍在积极制作《DEFECT》的完整原声音乐。这款小队制赛博朋克射击游戏由曾参与《毁灭战士》和《使命召唤》系列的资深开发者打造。2027年，他至少将在演出层面回归《毁灭战士》：他将作为英国RADAR音乐节的领衔嘉宾，首次与完整的现场乐队一起，演奏自己为《毁灭战士》和《毁灭战士：永恒》创作的音乐。

《毁灭战士》作曲者Mick Gordon拒绝使用AI

title: 《毁灭战士》作曲者Mick Gordon拒绝使用AI
text:
「去他的AI」
澳大利亚作曲家Mick Gordon以实验性的音乐创作手法备受推崇。在为2013年的《Killer Instinct》配乐时，他使用了刚洞（kangling）。这种藏族乐器传统上以人的股骨或胫骨雕制而成，让他得以用真正的骨头为骷髅角色Spinal创作主题曲。在为2016年的《毁灭战士》配乐时，他采样真实电锯声、打造独特吉他乐句的做法广为人知，也让游戏原声成为重金属杰作。不过，当被问及是否考虑过在创作过程中使用任何形式的生成式AI时，Gordon毫不含糊。借用已故歌手Meatloaf的歌词来说，为了创作出色的配乐，Gordon什么都愿意做，唯独这件事不行。
「去他妈的AI。」Gordon在2026年澳大利亚PAX展会接受IGN采访时说道。
玩家接下来将在10月14日发售的《战锤40K：爆矢枪2》中听到Gordon的作品。他为这款第一人称射击游戏的最终Boss战又创作了一首震撼到骨头里的劲曲，大家可以在下方预告片中试听。他也仍在全力创作《DEFECT》的配乐。这款赛博朋克题材小队射击游戏的开发团队由曾参与《毁灭战士》和《使命召唤》的资深开发者组成。粉丝可以放心，这两款游戏中的音乐都直接出自这位热爱金属乐的大师的头脑与指尖，而不是ChatGPT根据提示词生成的结果。
Gordon解释道：「生成式AI永远会落后于人类，因为从根本上说，它的训练素材就是人类已经创作出来的东西。它用训练素材建立一个庞大的数据库，然后根据这套数据得出一个非常符合逻辑的结论。但它始终会受限于自己的数据集。它永远不可能预测出接下来会出现什么、新的东西会是什么，或是人类能想出什么。仅凭这些系统的运作方式，就注定了它永远会落后。」
Gordon仍然乐观地相信，观众始终会被其他人类的作品吸引，而不是机器的作品。
Gordon说：「人类永远都会想与其他人类互动。永远如此。我觉得这些AI的东西，只会让人们有更多理由摆脱如今侵染我们生活的数字化。我觉得人类始终都会追求人与人之间的联系。」
喜欢Gordon作品的英国粉丝，将有机会与他本人建立这种人与人之间的联系。他将作为主打艺人登上2027年RADAR音乐节的舞台，届时会首次与完整乐队一起，现场演奏他为《毁灭战士》和《毁灭战士：永恒》创作的原声音乐。

text: 通过这次封闭式的沉浸体验，让我从故事、角色、武器升级，技能树成长等更全面的角度，感受到了《影之刃零》的野心，以及灵游坊这些年来对武侠朋克世界的精心雕琢。

title: 中国游戏口述史系列16：“目标出品，必属精品”，目标软件往事——张淳老师访谈
text:
背景信息
本文原载于微信公众号“ 游戏收藏与研究 ”。
原文标题 《“目标出品，必属精品”，目标软件往事——张淳老师访谈》 ，原作者“路行己”，经原作者及受访人授权，由 indienova 转载发布。
受访：张淳
访谈：路行己
访谈背景： 90 年代，有一家中国游戏公司因出品的游戏做到了款款精品而被玩家称为“中国暴雪”，这家公司就是目标软件。从 1998 至 2002 年，目标软件仅制作了《铁甲风暴》《傲世三国》和《秦殇》三款游戏，但每款游戏都足以载入史册。而本次，笔者有幸采访到了目标软件的负责人张淳老师（张老师），并记录了目标软件从 90 年代开始的单机游戏发展历程。
访谈时间： 2025 年 12 月 12 日
特别鸣谢： 谢成鸿、汤仲宁
（注：由于时间久远，受访者可能存在记忆偏差，如若与当时报道存在差异，则以当时报道为准）
美国之行
行己： 张老师能否介绍一下您是如何进入游戏行业的？
张老师： 我在哈工大学习计算机专业，当时我们大学毕业还是包分配的。毕业后，我就直接被分配到了航天部在上海的 509 研究所。92 年 10 月我在上海的一个招聘会上，通过了智冠公司的面试，随即加入了智冠在广州设立的工作室，印象中这家工作室可能是中国大陆第一家正版游戏公司。这个公司成立的背景应该跟智冠的《三国演义》大获成功有关。当时智冠为了开发更多游戏，于是决定在大陆开设分部，物色人才。
《三国演义》台版
北京收藏家协会游戏研究分会 路行己，实物藏品
这家工作室按照招聘地域下设了三个开发组，分别是北京组、上海组和广州组。由于我当时是从上海面试进入智冠的，所以就被分到上海组并负责全组的开发工作。记得我们开发的是一个 3D 飞行射击游戏。
行己： 这款游戏是类似《DOOM》的伪 3D 游戏么？
张老师： 不是 DOOM 那样的 2.5D 游戏，是一款真正的 3D 飞行射击游戏。而且开发难度非常高，当时没有 3D 游戏引擎，所有的 3D 程序都需要从零开发。我记得当时用 C 语言写了很多多边形演算、空间变换和矩阵运算的程序逻辑。这部游戏开发了 10 个月，不过最终没有发售。
编者按：真 3D 游戏代表《X 战机》和 2.5D 游戏代表《DOOM》的技术区别：

《X 战机》大陆引进版及《终极毁灭战士》大陆代理版
北京收藏家协会游戏研究分会 路行己，实物藏品
行己： 那您之后又制作了哪些项目？
张老师： 1994 年，智冠就开始在北京和上海设立新的分公司，我作为种子员工就去了上海，并且在那里认识了后来目标软件的投资人。当时这位英国投资人在美国投资了一家游戏公司，希望招聘 3 名程序员去美国做主机游戏的开发，所以我就借此机会去了美国，期间用了不到一年的时间，游戏就开发完成了。
行己： 所以您也算是中国大陆最早一批有海外游戏开发经验的人才？
张老师： 也算是有一点，我们当时是在硅谷的 Redwood City（红木城），印象中公司团队有 6、7 人。我们三位中国来的都是程序员，剩下的都是策划，美术主要是外包团队在做。
编者按：在《我不是玩家！——目标人物传奇：张淳》（新浪游戏报道，经笔者校对）中详细记录了张淳老师在美国的经历：
张淳离开了智冠，加盟了美国 DTMC 游戏发行公司。这家公司在硅谷，主要业务是发行 SFC 游戏。
“我在这里才算真正接触了游戏产业。我看见了很多美国的开发组，其实他们当时和我们现在有点相似，大部分所谓的制作公司都是几个年轻人凭着热情自己做产品，其中有实力的只是很少数，大多数还处于工作组的状态。”张淳讲起那段故事绘声绘色，“我经常正坐在公司里，一位朋克风格打扮的人，就背着一个破帆布包闯进来了，然后从包里拿出一个硬盘，开始演示他开发的游戏。挺神的！反正给你一种非常不规范的感觉。但当时我也接触了一些好的团队，比如做《暗黑破坏神》的那个开发小组就曾经到过 DTMC 给我们推荐《DIABLO》（暗黑破坏神）的原型。那个原型当时还非常粗糙呢，谁想到后来经过反复修改，竟能成了震惊世界的作品。”
《暗黑破坏神》及《地狱火》大陆代理版
北京收藏家协会游戏研究分会 路行己，实物藏品
但 DTMC 毕竟是一个小公司，虽然也出了十几个产品，可实际上只有一款叫《CALIFORNIA GAME》的滑雪游戏真正挣到钱了。后来，这个公司就倒了。不过 DTMC 的投资人没有完全放弃，他还想继续做游戏。这时，张淳等三名在 DTMC 工作的中国人就建议他把公司设在中国，投资人觉得不错，于是就请张淳他们回国组建了一个新的游戏开发公司。
编者按：从报道中可知，在 90 年代的美国，《暗黑破坏神》（1996 年 12 月 31 日）这种规模的游戏开发周期要 2 年左右。但是当时中国大量游戏的开发周期只有 6-12 个月，这也是国产游戏难出精品的一个原因。
创立目标软件
行己： 您回国以后成立的就是目标软件么？
张老师： 94 年底回国后我们最早先去了珠海，但是在那里招不到合适的人才，所以后来就来了北京。95 年 5 月，在北京成立的是目标树工作室，主要工作是给海外游戏厂商做技术外包。我们参与的两款游戏分别是《雷霆之蹄》和《Sports Pinball》，两部游戏的设计都是由海外团队负责，我们仅做技术支持，我当时负责《Sports Pinball》的技术开发。
行己： 听说您制作的这款弹珠游戏销量很好。
张老师： 是的，销量不错。这两个游戏制作完成以后我们还和清华幼儿园合作制作了教育软件，例如：《恬恬和小旋》。之所以选择做教育软件主要还是因为当时国内的教育软件市场要好一些。97 年的时候，我们发现国内游戏市场出现了大规模的增长，因此考虑自主开发游戏。当时公司更名为目标软件，下设三个工作室，其中奥世工作室负责游戏开发，我们制作的第一个游戏就是《铁甲风暴》。
编者按：关于清华期间的内容可参阅杨南征老师的访谈《爱国游戏之王，金盘游戏往事（上）——杨南征老师访谈》（成吉思汗部分）。
游戏性第一原则与《铁甲风暴》
《铁甲风暴》大盒版（张淳老师亲签）和海外版
北京收藏家协会游戏研究分会 路行己，实物藏品
行己： 您能否介绍一下《铁甲风暴》的立项思路？
张老师： 立项《铁甲风暴》主要是因为热爱和市场需求。我和团队里的很多人当时都非常喜欢玩《红警》，于是对即时战略游戏的机制设计和程序实现方式就有了比较深入的了解。此外更重要的是，即时战略游戏在 90 年代的 PC 平台上非常流行，拥有庞大的市场需求。所以最后我们选择了制作一款 RTS 游戏。
行己： 当时为何选择机甲题材，没有选择三国等市场规模更大的传统题材？
张老师： 这个和《铁甲风暴》的创新玩法有关系。因为《铁甲风暴》中各个作战单位都是由玩家选择的部件组合而成的，机甲题材最适合这种零件组装的概念。如果选择使用三国等历史题材，这个玩法创新就无法被有效的包装成合理的游戏规则概念了。我当时同意团队制作机甲题材的初衷也是源于内容要服务于游戏性的设计思路。
编者按：这里张淳老师给出了一个具有普遍意义的游戏设计问题解决思路：在游戏的玩法创意和故事设计上，如何做好平衡？特别是当二者出现冲突时应该如何取舍？从老师的答案中可以看出，对于偏重于策略的 RTS 游戏来说，他会优先从玩法乐趣出发，再选择合适的故事题材进行包装。如果我们再深入思考一下，不难发现，玩法与故事的优先级选择应该取决于游戏的卖点究竟是玩法创意还是剧情故事，设计者应该基于卖点来进行取舍。
行己： 《铁甲风暴》的单位组装玩法创新当时获得了非常好的市场反馈，在游戏玩法创新上有没有通用的经验？
张老师： 从《铁甲风暴》的角度来说，RTS 玩的主要是一些策略性的选择。它的底层策略主要是两个：生产和战斗。玩家在游戏里首先选的是先生产还是先战斗，对应到具体操作就是先提高产能还是先快速出兵，对应到战术就是先骚扰还是先抢矿，基本就是这样的自上而下的策略决策过程。《铁甲风暴》相当于在造兵这一层加了一层策略选择，就是玩家可以通过配件的研究和组装拥有更多的兵种搭配策略，这样就能让玩家玩到更丰富的策略内容，并且这些策略都围绕在前面提到的核心策略选择路径上。其实我们最早想的创新内容比后来实现的内容还要宏大。例如：玩家可以通过研究偏向于生产和战斗的机甲组件，来直接影响先生产还是先战斗的底层策略方向。此外在战斗科技方面，玩家还能选择偏重于速度、装甲、载重量等不同维度的机甲组件。在此之下，还能研究不同材质的防护装甲、不同移动方式的底盘、不同类型的武器等等，不过再往下做可能就过于复杂了，我们当时就没有继续深入了。
编者按：关于《铁甲风暴》策划相关的内容请参见 《铁甲风暴往事，制作人汤仲宁先生访谈》
行己： 《铁甲风暴》在发售前一年，还去了美国 E3？
张老师： 是的，是我亲自去的。
张淳老师谈 97 年参加 E3 展览的情况
《家用电脑与游戏机创刊五周年白金典藏本》
编者按：1997 年《铁甲风暴》以 DEMO 的形式登陆了美国 E3 大展，同期还有被台湾厂商带去的《生死之间》，这两款游戏是目前已知最早登陆 E3 展览的大陆自研游戏。
行己： 铁甲风暴还有过海外版本的代理，这里您还有印象吗？
张老师： 印象不深了，可能都是打包授权出去的。
铁甲风暴海外代理情况报道
《大众软件》（1999.10）
行己： 请问《铁甲风暴》的市场表现如何？
张老师： 整个游戏的开发成本在 100 万左右，游戏 OEM 版最终在中国销量达到了 30 万，这个在当时应该算是不错的成绩。
编者按：1999 年大陆电脑总销量约为 400 万台，其中约 120 万台电脑为家用自购，进而可以估算出，当时约有 1/4 的家用电脑装有《铁甲风暴》OEM 版。这无疑是一个极高的市场份额，也为推动《铁甲风暴》成为经典游戏 IP，起到了重要作用。
行己： 请问大盒版（零售版）《铁甲风暴》的发行量您还有印象吗？
张老师： 大盒版我印象比较深的是有一万多套。因为担心游戏刚上市就被盗版，所以我们从压盘到后来包装环节都尽量亲历亲为，这一万多套的大盒版都是我们在公司自己包装的，所以印象特别深刻。不过后面的应该也找厂家代工生产过，主要是因为卖火了，自己包装不过来。特别是有了 OEM 版以后，盗版的优势也就不大了。
报道中提及的大盒版销量
《目标：为世界打造中国的"游戏大片"》（新浪游戏）
《铁甲风暴》登顶连邦软件月销排行榜
连邦软件销售排行（1998.04.28-05.24）
铁甲风暴在玩家票选榜排名第 4
《大众软件》龙虎榜（1998.10）
编者按：结合作者收藏情况，发现《铁甲风暴》大盒版确实存在两个版本，主要在包装的细微差别上。此外，根据《铁甲风暴》零售版销量 17000 套的数据，推断大盒版发行量总共在 2-3 万套。另有报道称《铁甲风暴》初期的销量甚至超过了《魔兽争霸 2》陆版。值得注意的是，《铁甲风暴》取得这些优秀市场成绩时，正处于“血狮事件”出现不久之后，中国玩家对国产游戏信心不足的时期。所以国内玩家对《铁甲风暴》的认可，也说明该作极大的恢复了玩家对国产游戏的信心。这是《铁甲风暴》的又一个重要历史意义：挽救了中国玩家对国产游戏的信心。

《国内原创游戏评比》（大众软件 1999.01）
国产出海大成之作《傲世三国》
《傲世三国》（张淳老师亲签）和资料片《三分天下》
北京收藏家协会游戏研究分会 路行己，实物藏品
行己： 《铁甲风暴》取得成功后，目标为何没有开发续作，而是选择了《傲世三国》？
张老师： 《铁甲风暴》当时确实受到了关注，不过在营收方面，也还属于只能维持公司运营的水平，所以我认为机甲题材的市场受众还是不大，于是就希望从题材入手来做拥有更大市场规模的游戏。我们团队当时商量了一下，三国题材应该是最适合的。因为这个题材在中国乃至海外都有极大的受众群体，而且也非常适合制作成 RTS 游戏，沿用我们在《铁甲风暴》上的技术积累。于是我们就立项了《傲世三国》。
行己： 我记得《傲世三国》还有不少创新内容，例如内外城的设计等等。
张老师： 对，我们比较自豪的一点就是，目标制作的每个游戏都不是简单的拷贝，《傲世三国》里就首创了很多内容，像是通过双层地图还原战略与战术层的三国体验，在局部战斗上可以爬攻城梯爬上城墙战斗，在经济收入上采用中国的赋税制度，还拥有自然灾害等设计，以及基于这些创新内容重新设计的各种 AI 算法。我印象比较深的就是因为当时创新的内容比较多，使得游戏会出一些很离奇的 BUG。为此，我和另一位同事还专门飞去英国的 Eidos 修改了一个导致游戏崩溃的 BUG。我记得那个 BUG 就是因为电脑指挥的士兵将攻城梯搭到了地图外面，导致游戏直接崩溃了。说起来这个 BUG 之前为何没有发现呢？其实是因为它是程序在实现一系列创新玩法时叠加产生的偶发情况。
行己： 傲世三国是否沿用了《铁甲风暴》的技术？
张老师： 沿用了一部分技术，但我们在原有的技术基础上做了大幅的迭代。《铁甲风暴》和《傲世三国》的寻路算法与战斗 AI 都是我写的，因为《傲世三国》增加了水路、攻城梯等新的地形介质，还有新的战斗规则，使得《铁甲风暴》里的寻路和 AI 算法都无法直接复用到《傲世三国》上。因为这些新的规则使得 NPC 并不知道怎么才能用最优的方法去攻击玩家，它既不能基于新的规则发现玩家战术上的薄弱点，也无法利用不同的地形介质和载具发现最优的进攻路径。例如：遇到水路使用船舶，遇到城墙使用云梯等。所以《傲世三国》在技术上需要加入大量新的算法逻辑。我记得当时最基本的一个寻路算法叫 A 星算法。其实我并不知道这个算法在国外的 RTS 游戏中已经应用，当时纯粹是从软件设计专业的角度出发，自己研究出的如何将此算法应用到我们的游戏中。特别是《傲世三国》更加复杂的地图规则，使得我们的算法也更加复杂，这些都是需要单独开发的新内容，而且这些程序设计在当时都是没有参考的，毕竟从玩法机制上我们就已经与其他 RTS 游戏有很大不同了。
行己： 当时《傲世三国》的创新内容是怎么想出来的呢？
张老师： 主要还是大家集思广益，我最后拍板。另外当时我们都比较关注游戏创意。那个时候整个行业还处于野蛮生长时期，大家其实没有那么强的商业性，虽然我们也有营收压力，不过有投资支持，所以也没有去想赚快钱。例如用《铁甲风暴》的技术快速开发一款换皮三国的产品。本质上那时候大家更多地还是出于兴趣与热爱去做游戏，不愿意做这种特别商业化的决定，所以在公司层面和员工层面上都是非常鼓励内容创新的一个氛围。
行己： 《傲世三国》的市场表现如何？
张老师： 《傲世三国》在国内由连邦软件签订了 10 万套包销合同，最后零售版的销量有 12 万套，在海外是 Eidos 负责发行，销量有 26 万套，这里包含了 16 国语言版本。
《傲世三国》国内销量
《过去、现在、将来—连邦游戏产品部纵横谈》（新浪游戏）
行己： 您认为是什么因素使《傲世三国》零售版的国内销量比《铁甲风暴》提升了近 10 倍？
张老师： 第一是题材上的优势，三国题材的受众要比机甲和科幻题材大；第二是游戏品质，我们基于三国的题材做了很多符合三国体验的玩法创新；第三是国民收入提升，2000 年初盗版游戏也很多，但是我们将游戏的价格下调后，越来越多的玩家开始支持正版，因为大家手里有钱了，只要游戏品质够好，玩家们更愿意支持正版游戏了。所以这里还是要感谢中国经济发展和中国玩家的民族情怀。
行己： 《傲世三国》在海外的发行情况怎么样？
张老师： 《傲世三国》海外整体代理给了 Eidos，具体的情况我并不了解。

《秦殇》首发版（张淳老师亲签）

行己： 从公司层面上讲，当时为何没有继续制作 RTS 游戏，而是同意立项 RPG 游戏《秦殇》？
张老师： 其实这也是一个顺应市场潮流的选择，我当时认为 RPG 游戏，特别是 ARPG 游戏的市场规模要比 RTS 游戏更大，所以就改为制作 RPG 游戏。
行己： 请问《秦殇》的开发过程是什么样的呢？
张老师： 此时我的重点已经在公司管理上，因此没有直接参与《秦殇》的开发。不过为了保障游戏品质，这个团队的人才配置在当时可以算是明星阵容了。我印象中策划是从《傲世三国》过来的刘豫斌，还有后来加入的刘铁（已故《天龙八部》主策划）、刘勇。主美是刘坤（后像素软件负责人），程序总监是刘刚（原前导瞬间工作室负责人）。

行己： 目标当时是如何招到这么多优秀人才的？
张老师： 我觉得主要还是因为《铁甲风暴》和《傲世三国》取得了成功，使得很多游戏人才都愿意来目标软件工作。其次我们会考察应聘者的工作态度和工作能力。从工作态度上来说，在当时的大环境下，开发游戏在社会上还属于一个比较边缘化的工作，收入也不算高，因此能够顶住各方舆论，不计较收入的应聘者，大多是有决心做好这份工作的。最后在能力考察方面，我主要负责技术岗位的招聘，我这边基本看一下对方写的代码就可以确定是否能够入职。
行己： 《秦殇》的销售情况您还有印象么？
张老师： 具体不是很清楚了，估计在 20-30 万套。
行己： 《秦殇》在海外的发售情况如何？
张老师： 《秦殇》在海外采用了分地区代理的形式，这样可以让我们与擅长不同地区发行的多家代理商合作，进而提升游戏的营收规模。不过现在对于游戏在海外的销售情况我已经记不清了。

30 年后回看游戏设计
行己： 在开发出这么多款精品游戏后，您认为如何思考才能创造出好的游戏？
张老师： 我理解要想做出好游戏首先需要对游戏的本质有一定的认识。简单来讲，游戏就是给玩家设立一系列挑战，玩家通过不同的方法完成挑战并获得奖励的过程。在这个过程中玩家需要运用智力、操作或者知识的方法来完成挑战，到了网游时代，玩家还可以通过组织方法来完成挑战。如果一个游戏能够在挑战规则和奖励形式的设计上，让玩家以更有趣的形式运用这些方法完成挑战，那么这个游戏在玩法吸引力上就有了基本保障。如果能够再用好的世界观进行包装，那么游戏的成功率就会大大提升。
行己： 所以我们每一次的创新成功都是在要完成的挑战上和挑战方法上做差异化？
张老师： 是的，其实就是策划如何去设计解决问题的手段。例如：RTS 游戏解决问题的手段基本都在造兵和战术上，那么战术如何多样化，差异化就是一些创新点，这些点背后考察的是玩家的智力还是操作。如果只是单一的看谁造兵快，那么就是一个很同质化的方法，但是如果在不同维度设计出差异化的兵种，互相克制的兵种，那么就给玩家在战术层面丰富了解决问题的方法。还可以在更高层面思考，包括生产层面等等。如果我们再把这些设计拆分到考核对应的智力、操作等方法上，就能分析出当玩家运用这些规则完成挑战时的兴奋感。
行己： 所以说像《塞尔达荒野之息》通过化学引擎，给玩家提供了新的完成挑战的方法是不是就属于这种情况？
张老师： 是的，其实就是给玩家很多样化的方法，让他通过运用自己的智慧、操作等手段以一种很新鲜的方式完成挑战的过程，这个过程就能带给玩家极高的兴奋感。
行己： 是不是可以认为《铁甲风暴》和《傲世三国》都属于这个设计思路下的产物，因为虽然他们都在 RTS 游戏模式里，但是他们在战术方法上都有创新，例如：机甲单位组合、攻城梯攻城这些战术手段。
张老师： 是的，可以这么理解。其实《秦殇》也是在这个思路下加入的五行属性规则。不过这种依靠玩家通过自身能力去完成挑战的游戏形式到了网游时代大多数都被简化成了数值和属性。这也是网络游戏和单机游戏在体验乐趣上很大的差别。
行己： 是的，这个和网游还有 F2P 游戏的商业模式有很大关系。
张老师： 对，不过网游要是能够做出类似单机游戏这种新鲜的挑战完成方法的话，应该会更好。因为我觉得游戏的内核还是应该要让玩家能够感受到自己投入思考和精力后来带的优势感。所以现在我在跟策划开会的时候也不断强调要给玩家构建出行为价值，让玩家能够切实的感受到通过自己的行为可以在游戏中获得优势，而不是所有的好处都在商城里。
行己： 游戏行业现在的内容付费应该是解决了类似的问题？
张老师： 对的，现在很多网游开始在做体验付费，而不是付费变强了，这种就更偏向于早期单机游戏的做法。而且这种体验型付费的游戏生命周期会更长。
行己： 除了玩法和内容的设计，目标软件的几部单机作品在完成度上在当时也是处于国内领先水平的，这点是如何做到的呢？
张老师： 其实这点上我们当时也只是按照成熟的软件开发流程来制作而已，并没有太多的诀窍。如果有一些优势的话，可能就是我们当时应该是国内比较少的，有完整软件和游戏开发经验的团队，所以在质量把控方面有一些相对成熟的做法。不过现在游戏行业已经很成熟了，大家开发的游戏完成度都很高了。
行己： 好的，谢谢您！
后记：“目标出品，必属精品”
2000 年初，美国暴雪公司因《星际争霸》、《魔兽争霸》、《暗黑破坏神》的成功，被中国玩家盛赞为“暴雪出品，必属精品”。而另一个让中国玩家感到自豪的是目标软件百分百的游戏精品率和《傲世三国》、《秦殇》在海内外取得的成功，让中国玩家也喊出了“目标出品，必属精品”的口号。
相应的，在一次采访中张淳老师也谈到：“我们宁可开发得慢一些，制作周期长一些，但一定要保证产品的质量。因为我觉得质量是游戏软件最根本的一个问题。与其一年做两三款产品，不如多花点时间打造一个精品——从销量上说，这一个精品可能顶得上一堆普通产品的总和，同时它还能在玩家中赢得口碑，为以后的产品发行铺路。” 这段话背后表达了张淳老师对国产单机游戏行业的思考：在当时盗版泛滥的中国，只有制作出国际化品质的游戏，通过全球发行，才能实现单机游戏的盈利。
如果我们追溯回 1998 年，彼时的目标软件仅有一款游戏——《铁甲风暴》。当同期的大部分游戏公司都将开发周期设定在 6 至 12 个月时，这款开发了 2 年的 RTS 游戏凭借其过硬的素质直接开启了全球化发行的道路。而更值得自豪的是，在这个思路下，目标软件从《铁甲风暴》开始，就实现了正版游戏的盈利。这在盗版泛滥的 90 年代末中国游戏市场堪称行业奇迹。
业内关于《铁甲风暴》盈利的讨论（销量非最终数字）
《国产游戏何去何从大讨论》（大众软件 1999.02）
到了 2000 年初，随着《傲世三国》和《秦殇》的上市，目标软件依靠精品化战略，不仅在盈利能力上得到了进一步提升，也在玩家群体中获得了良好的口碑。从当今视角来看，此时的目标软件不仅同时拥有三个自主开发的游戏 IP，还树立了良好的公司品牌形象，并且成为了当时最成功的中国出海游戏企业。有趣的是，带领团队取得这些成就的张淳老师却自称并不是一个狂热的游戏爱好者。一次采访中他提到：“我确实和很多游戏人都不同。我并不是一个特别纯粹、对游戏特别有热情的玩家，但是我做事情一向比较认真，不管什么事只要作起来就一定要把他做好，所以虽然我接触游戏有一定的偶然性，但操作起来后我一直都把他作为自己的一个事业。对于游戏，我不是因为喜欢它而去做他，玩游戏的时候也没有什么特殊的想法，但是做起来以后我产生了一种强烈的要把他做好的愿望。实际上对于目标而言，我们有很多东西也是在做的过程中不断发掘不断培养出来的。喜欢其实真的不是最重要的，因为兴趣与热情只能维持一小段时间，只有你把他当成是一个事业并且建立起一个规范的秩序，你才能很有序地发展下去。由己推人，我现在招人也并不是看他对游戏有多热爱，有多喜欢，有多投入，而是看他做事业的那种责任心与恒心怎么样。这才是最关键的。”
也许正是这种非玩家心态的游戏管理者，使得目标软件走出了精品化路线，并挺过了 90 年代末的中国游戏公司倒闭潮，而也正是这种客观冷静的观察方式，让目标软件在后来的发展中，果断转型成网络游戏公司，开发出多款获奖作品。躲过了网络游戏对单机市场的碾压式冲击。
《傲世 Online》与《天骄》的获奖证书
张淳老师提供，实物照片
1995 至 2025，经历了 30 年的市场变化和时代变迁，昔日的目标软件如今已经成为以网络游戏为主的目标在线。而这一切都源于 1992 年张淳老师在上海参加的那场游戏招聘会，源于 1996 年 7 月奥世工作室的成立。
目标软件奥世工作室早期成员介绍
《月之暗面，国内知名游戏制作组访谈（上）》（大众软件 1998.05）
部分游戏的历史意义与收藏价值
《铁甲风暴》
开发周期：2 年
上市时间：1998.05
陆版大盒版发行量：预估 2-3 万套（已知销量 1.7 万）
历史意义及收藏价值
1、90 年代国产精品游戏的代表之一；
2、90 年代市场反馈最成功的国产 RTS 游戏；
3、首批登陆 E3 展览的大陆自研游戏；
4、中国最早出海的机甲题材游戏；
5、挽回了中国玩家因“血狮事件”对国产游戏失去的信心；
6、全品实物存世量稀少。
《傲世三国》
开发周期：3 年
上市时间：2000 年 12 月
陆版大盒版发行量：15 万套左右（销量：12 万套）
历史意义及收藏价值
1、第一个在全球市场取得成功的大陆自研游戏；
2、中国文化游戏题材成功出海的代表作之一；
3、首个获得国家电子出版物奖的游戏；
4、代表同时期中国 RTS 游戏设计最高水平。
《秦殇》
开发周期：3 年
上市时间：2002 年 7 月
陆版大盒版发行量：30 万套左右
历史意义及收藏价值
1、目前已知中国自研的第一款 DRPG 游戏；
2、该作的联网模式使其成为代表中国由单机时代向网游时代过渡的节点性游戏；
3、目前仍代表了中国在 DRPG 方面的最高设计水平；
4、中国唯一取得巨大影响力的秦文化游戏 IP；
5、中国第一款以秦朝文化背景成功出海的游戏。
——全文完——

title: 本周 Steam 值得关注的游戏 10.12 - 10.18（一）
text:
本周将迎来 Steam 的“烹饪游戏节”，一起来看看新发售的游戏吧！
注： 本系列文章的信息主要整合自 Steam 与 SteamDB 的即将发售列表，由于 Steam 支持手动输入日期及发售、同步不及时等原因，本列表可能会遗漏收录一些作品的发售信息。如果本周有您的作品或您喜欢的作品未被列出，欢迎直接评论补充链接～～
塔防山贼模拟器（Bandit Simulator TD）
关键字： AI 生成内容、塔防、挂机游戏、刷宝
发行日期： 2026/10/12（ 中文支持 ）
这是一款"塔防战斗+山门经营+放置挂机"的游戏。从无到有，建立一座土匪山寨。以塔防(TowerDefense)为核心模式。拦路抢劫、狩猎妖兽、探索地图，招募华夏名将！职业、装备、修炼境界，培养强力角色！研究、建造、锻造、炼丹、种田、采集等技艺，不断发展山寨，最终攻伐城池，占领天下！让"上头爽快"与"简单轻松"并存！
同情共焚（Burn With Me）
关键字： 牌组构建式类 Rogue、剧情丰富
发行日期： 2026/10/12（ 中文支持 ）
《同情共焚》是一款叙事驱动的牌组构筑游戏，讲述一个个充满神秘色彩的故事，闲适氛围背后暗藏恐惧。你那满怀危险激情的老师将引导你完成禁忌的古老仪式。有时，召唤心魔才是自我治愈的唯一良方。
怪奇餐厅（Life, the Universe, and Restaurants）
关键字： 管理、烹饪、建造
发行日期： 2026/10/12（ 中文支持 ）
在怪奇宇宙经营餐厅，为所谓的“神明”制作佳肴！点单、备菜、烹饪、上菜，收银，支付租金，购买设备，扩张地皮，部署各种各样的机器人，实现自动化后厨，把手忙脚乱变成高效运转。而你，就负责“斩杀”那些自诩为神的客人。
间谍密令外传（Spy Drops Gaiden）
关键字： 潜行、动作、复古
发行日期： 2026/10/12（ 中文支持 ）
潜入敌人基地，执行一系列隐秘任务，体验令人血脉偾张的经典老派 2D 潜行动作游戏。
The Doll Shop
关键字： 恐怖、剧情丰富、选择取向
发行日期： 2026/10/12（ 中文支持 ）
《The Doll Shop》是一款以手绘风格为主的叙事游戏，糅合了浪漫与惊悚元素。舞台设定在日本乡间一条被雪封的村落，你将化身年轻的人偶匠，于阴冷诡谲的村中与儿时故友重逢，你敢揭露那个不为人知的秘密吗？
Space Manager
关键字： 太空模拟、策略
发行日期： 2026/10/12（暂无中文）
参与真实的太空任务，管理经济，探索太阳系。在地球上建造并扩建你的航天中心，承接合同，并将卫星送入轨道。通过研究、适应并收集有价值的科学数据，开启你日益壮大的航空航天帝国。
Den-Den: Tokyo Horror
关键字： 恐怖、角色扮演、开放世界
发行日期： 2026/10/12（ 中文支持 ）
《Den-Den: Tokyo Horror》是一款事件实时展开的日式恐怖 RPG。在这座你的每一个选择都会影响周遭世界的城市里，熬过一夜。今晚，你会为多少人的死亡负责？
Barfender: CO-OP Bar Simulator
关键字： 在线合作、模拟、资源管理、欢乐
发行日期： 2026/10/12（ 中文支持 ）EA
《Barfender》是一款混乱的合作酒吧模拟游戏。你要倒酒、清理灾难、阻止打架，并在一切崩坏时努力让酒吧撑下去。建好场子，服务人群，熬过这一夜。
别眨眼（Time To Wake Up）
关键字： 剧情丰富、悬疑、冒险、心理
发行日期： 2026/10/12（ 中文支持 ）
自以为挣脱梦境？不，你只是睁开双眼，触碰内心深处那段未竟的旅程。 在《别眨眼》中，你将踏入梦境与现实交错的世界。在呓语的引导下，重组环境、解开谜题、追寻记忆碎片，面对孤独、恐惧与过去的阴影。每一次眨眼，都将成为自我发现与成长的契机。层层梦境，种种阻挠，你能否摆脱迷失，找回真实的自我？
Battleplan
关键字： 即时战略、二战
发行日期： 2026/10/12（暂无中文）
《Battleplan》是一款历史向二战即时战略游戏，拥有无与伦比的真实感和模拟度。玩家可以在基于真实地理数据打造而成的庞大战场上尽情作战。自定义作战序列和指挥链，组建属于你的军队。直接在地图上进行绘制，制定周密的作战计划，并交给麾下军官执行。
音刃法则（Alpha Nomos）
关键字： 动作类 Rogue、节奏、砍杀
发行日期： 2026/10/12（ 中文支持 ）
是时候以节拍为刃了！化身切萝，闯入被乐音扭曲的绚烂世界，斩碎暴走的人偶大军。战斗随原声脉动——踩着节拍出招，将连击谱成旋律，上演一场艳惊四座、编排完美的华丽混乱！
猫咪花园 Meow Garden
关键字： 农场模拟、生物收集
发行日期： 2026/10/12（ 中文支持 ）
欢迎来到猫猫岛！在这款温馨治愈的农场模拟游戏中，猫咪会从土里破土而出！播下种子、长出猫咪，邂逅超过 40 种不同品种的小可爱。布置家园、训练猫咪、完成订单，打造属于你的猫咪庄园。
The Traveller's Sight
关键字： 指向点击、冒险、全动态影像
发行日期： 2026/10/12（暂无中文）
拥有超自然能力的调查员文森特·杜马斯被派往法国一个拥有扑朔迷离历史的小镇，调查劳伦·德尔加多之死的真相。他利用自己与亡灵沟通的能力，着手寻找能将他引向凶手的线索。
BABEL: Invent a Way
关键字： AI 生成内容、在线合作、解谜、冒险
发行日期： 2026/10/12（ 中文支持 ）
禁止使用现有语言。只能通过「↑」「↓」「←」「→」「・」这五个符号进行交流，交换彼此掌握的信息，推进魔法仪式，并以解除封印为目标。起初明明只是五个简单的符号，却会随着一次次交流，逐渐成长为只属于你们两人的、独一无二的语言。 ※仅支持双人游玩
Doodle Steel
关键字： AI 生成内容、策略、模拟、物理
发行日期： 2026/10/12（ 中文支持 ）
画出来，派出去，看它开战。在这款兵线对战策略游戏中，每个单位都是你亲手画出的涂鸦：画出车体、履带、火炮和气球，在 108 个二战战场上摧毁敌方基地。
Ward Off Evil
关键字： 角色扮演、策略
发行日期： 2026/10/12（暂无中文）
《Ward Off Evil》是一款以末日剑与魔法世界为背景的开放世界策略角色扮演游戏。创建你的角色，集结军队，在废土上四处游荡，为阻止或引发循环的终结而战。
深馅地牢（Deep Dish Dungeon）
关键字： 在线合作、迷宫探索、烹饪、生存
发行日期： 2026/10/13（ 中文支持 ）
这款生存探索游戏中，银河恶魔城风味与制作要素巧妙融合。你将在精心设计的地牢中冒险解谜。既可单枪匹马，也能与好友联机组队，深入地牢深处，破解重重谜团。
HYPERFIGHT 2
关键字： 2D 格斗
发行日期： 2026/10/13（暂无中文）EA
你的能量条就是你的生命。在这款全新风格的 2D 格斗游戏中，明智地使用它，否则将面临失去一切的风险。这就是《HYPERFIGHT》的下一代进化！
驱灵天师（Ghost hunter）
关键字： 撤离射击、在线合作、神话
发行日期： 2026/10/13（ 中文支持 ）EA
一款融合国风民俗、神话志怪的多人联机 PVE 搜打撤游戏，你将化身神通各异的天师使用各类法宝，符箓，道具，完成各类民俗事件任务，与队友探索被邪祟入侵的场景降妖捉鬼，收集物资道具宝物，诛灭各路妖魔鬼怪，体验沉浸式中式除祟冒险。
Monkey Bizniz
关键字： 在线合作、物理、欢乐
发行日期： 2026/10/13（暂无中文）
和朋友联机合作，为猴王的盛宴收集香蕉! 装满推车，冲上山顶! 出了事别甩锅给队友。
Horns of Deliverance
关键字： 第一人称射击、动作类 Rogue、迷幻
发行日期： 2026/10/13（暂无中文）EA
《Horns of Deliverance》是一款第一人称动作类 Roguelike 游戏，拥有真实感十足的射击体验，玩家需要摄入致幻物质，以防止脑芯片接管身体。
月霜（Moonfrost）
关键字： 农场模拟、农场模拟、冒险
发行日期： 2026/10/13（ 中文支持 ）EA
在这个饱受陨石风暴摧残的世界里，以猎霜者的身份踏上一段温馨又壮阔的旅程吧！重建破碎的村庄，享受耕作、制作以及与可爱邻居们结下友谊的生活，同时揭开神秘“第二月亮”背后的黑暗真相。
ROLLA
关键字： 破坏、恶人主角、竞分
发行日期： 2026/10/13（暂无中文）
突发新闻！市中心正遭到一团不断蠕动、闪烁着光芒的肉团的肆虐！目击者将现场描述为“一场充满嘎吱声的街机式破坏，生存与追逐高分在此交织！”。这究竟是什么生物！？它的动机是什么！？它真的是这里的反派吗！？现在将画面切回演播室。
Spoofs Playland
关键字： 装饰、小游戏、教育
发行日期： 2026/10/13（暂无中文）
玩耍、收集、装饰！《Spoofs Playland》是一款轻松休闲、适合全家同乐的点击式迷你游戏合集，你将在这个色彩斑斓的世界中收集装饰品，并与 Spoofs 建立深厚的情感纽带。赚取奖励、完成任务、购买新背景和数百种物品，打造你梦想中的房间吧！
闹鬼大劫掠（Haunted Heist）
关键字： 社交聚会游戏、动作、劫掠、欢乐
发行日期： 2026/10/13（ 中文支持 ）
《闹鬼大劫掠》是一款支持 3-8 人对局的恐怖派对游戏。盗宝者需要在随机生成的宅邸中搜集宝石；捣蛋鬼则要用各式各样的技能来吓唬、干扰、消灭盗宝者，保护自己的家园。
LampMan!
关键字： 2D 平台、动作
发行日期： 2026/10/13（暂无中文）
《LampMan!》是一款 2D 动作平台游戏，拥有三位可操控角色，可随时在他们之间切换。掌握他们的技能，征服色彩斑斓的关卡，让灯之世界重见光明吧！
第二部分
下一部分明日送上！

title: RPGs are simply better when you're an idiot
text:
Dungeon Master
(Image credit: Future) Welcome to Dungeon Master , PC Gamer's regular RPG column, where Online Editor Fraser Brown delves into PC gaming's most beloved and enduring genre. Grab a seat in our badly-lit tavern and please ignore the goblin puke.
Most videogame RPGs are selling a power fantasy—the idea that you are competent, clever and regardless of the odds will still manage to save the day. Fate has made you a hero, and nothing is going to stop you from achieving your goals. And this holds a lot of appeal. It's sometimes nice to be able to take a holiday from my own incompetence.
Over the last few days I've managed to drop my dinner, get trapped on a bus going in the wrong direction, get peed on by a dog, get almost run over by a car and, to top it all off, actually get knocked over by an electric scooter. I am a walking disaster.
(Image credit: BioWare) Geralt never gets peed on. Shepard never lands on their arse after colliding with a teen. These are not heroic moments. When these protagonists face adversity, it only serves as an excuse for more badass adventures.
It turns out, though, that constantly winning becomes a little dull. I want more friction. More fuck ups. But games, by and large, want you to succeed, even when they throw obstacles in your way. Last month, I wrote about how The Blood of Dawnwalker sets up all these possible ways for you to fail, only to then make it almost impossible to screw up unless you're really trying. But it's hardly alone in this regard.
But this problem is not inherent to all RPGs—it's certainly not present in TTRPGs, which tend to embrace misfortune. Many of them actually thrive on it, like Mothership and Call of Cthulhu. And it was only when I started to play TTRPGs that I really began to appreciate how much fun it is to not be the Chosen One, to just be some guy who, either through cursed rolls or bad calls, keeps messing up.
Idiots have more fun
(Image credit: Larian) Being asked to do a thing, doing the thing, and then getting congratulated for it—that's not a particularly good anecdote. If, in the process of completing your quest, you get outsmarted by some children, throw up all over yourself, break your foot and end up disappointing everyone around you, well, then you've got a great story.
Thankfully, more and more RPGs are celebrating idiots. Not that it's a new concept. I vividly recall the shock I got when, after a series of questionable decisions in Baldur's Gate 2, my stoic pal Jaheira decided that I was so rotten, so beyond hope, that the only solution was to kill me.
It's absolutely more prevalent now, however, as CRPGs have started leaning into their TTRPG roots in more dramatic ways. Baldur's Gate 3 is still a power fantasy, but it's one driven by dice rolls, where failure is always nipping at your heels. Play the Dark Urge and you'll even start accidentally murdering people.
(Image credit: ZA/UM) Disco Elysium is, of course, the RPG that most embraces the idea that it's fun to be shit. Even if you're the luckiest player in the world, nailing every roll, you can still simply choose to be a big dumb weirdo. I base most of my decisions on how funny I think the writing is going to be, which is how I ended up a communist paranormal investigator constantly going on rants about the apocalypse.
When failure is almost guaranteed, it makes succeeding so much more impressive.
Zero Parades and Esoteric Ebb have followed suit—two games where every interaction offers you the tantalising prospect of making a complete tit out of yourself. In the former, I managed to have a full-on breakdown during a phone call in the first five minutes. In the latter, I largely ignored my quest to solve an act of terrorism to instead focus all of my energy on winning an election where I was not a candidate.
What I find so endlessly compelling about these kinds of RPGs is not necessarily the constant cock ups, though. It's more that they offer up a ridiculous breadth of options, making me feel like anything could happen. You can pick the most ridiculous actions or dialogue choices, and there's still the chance that you'll nail them, pulling off something seemingly impossible. When failure is almost guaranteed, it makes succeeding so much more impressive.
Critical fail
(Image credit: Warhorse Studios) And if you do mess up, or more likely when, it feels like you're getting more story, more interesting consequences. How a game handles failure is so important. If it gives you all these ways to get it wrong, but then simply punishes or kills you, it implies that there's only really one right way to do things—you're either a flawless hero or you're dead.
I recall a quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2 where I had to set up a tournament between two swordfighting schools, which involved a bit of larceny. I got caught, became embroiled in a Benny Hill-style chase, and while I managed to get out with the stolen goods, nobody could really call it a success. The result? Everyone knew I did the crime. The tournament went forward, but my team was given a serious handicap. When we won, it felt so much more meaningful because my actions had turned us into the underdogs.
Good roleplaying is essentially improv. What you want is a permissive GM (whether it's a literal GM or a videogame's systems) who's down for a bit of "Yes, and," who will let you come up with a dumb solution and try to find interesting outcomes even if you fail miserably. This way, the storytelling becomes truly collaborative, full of texture and surprises, rather than yet another rote hero's journey.

title: Arc Raiders 2.0 is here, and you can finally turn those lights on your backpack off
text:
I remember being a kid and wishing I had shoes that lit up. I know now that I was a fool. If I festooned myself with garish lights, how would I scavenge for supplies in a frozen wasteland without being spotted by strangers who may or may not kill me before I can use my grappling hook to get away? This isn't a real problem I have, nor is it a real problem Arc Raiders players will have anymore, since your backpack now has an emissive toggle.
That's one of many little overhauls that arrived in Embark Studios' popular extraction shooter Thursday, and you can read all about the rest in the 2.0 patch notes . If you've not been tuned into the extraction world as of late, you did indeed read that right: Arc Raiders has gotten a big shakeup with the Frozen Trails update , which comes bearing snowy mountains and grappling hooks.
But that's not what's exciting about patch notes—the best part of combing through each little bullet point is seeing all those long-awaited bug fixes and little quality-of-life changes like the aforementioned emissive toggle for backpacks. That and tidbits like "added mouth animation for when players are talking in proximity chat," which I can only hope looks as silly in-game as it does in my imagination.
Some other big, but also small changes include the fact that you can open the map when you're downed now, new contextual animations for a variety of things (your character should look more exhausted when sprinting for a while), and an increased max stash size: 328 without expedition bonuses.
Snowy and desolate as it might look, Arc Raiders seems to be picking up momentum with the new update. Its average player count has gone way up recently, probably due to the free weekend that's going on right now, so it seems like as good a time as any to dive back in if you're so inclined. If that's you, try out our guides on how to arc raid with the best of 'em.

title: Nier creator Yoko Taro says he's achieved his career dreams, but he continues working because it's 'good for preventing dementia'
text:
They say that art is never finished, only abandoned—but that doesn't seem to be the case for Yoko Taro, creator of Nier and Drakengard, who you might recognize by the round, smiley Emil mask he wears. According to a report from Denfaminicogamer (via IGN ), Taro said at the Tokyo French Institute last month that he's already more or less realized his vision and has considered retiring.
"With Drakengard, the first game I was given the opportunity to direct, I was actually able to do almost everything the way I wanted," Taro said. "As a game otaku, I think the dream is to release something you've always wanted to create into the world. Having achieved that dream, I view everything after that as the remainder of my life."
As for why he continues to work in gamedev if he's already achieved his dreams, well, he said the money doesn't hurt—and that he has a fear of how his mental health might degrade should he grow idle. "This is good for preventing dementia," he said.
It's worth noting that Taro is, to put it in technical terms, a bit of a silly goose, if the mask didn't tip you off. As the IGN report notes, it's possible he doesn't literally mean that he only works in gamedev to stave off dementia. But that sentiment, as well as his saying that he hopes he can dodge the "flames" of competition from younger, AI-assisted generations before he dies, speak to how Taro views his place in the games industry.
"I've always worked in the games industry with the mindset of 'filling in the gaps.' I really like games like Ico and Ikaruga, but when I played them they were so perfect that I thought, 'I don't need to make games in these genres,'" he said.
"That's not jealousy, it's the feeling of, 'This gap has already been filled, so I need to fill a different one.' I think the reason that my games are crude games full of terrible things is because the pioneers have already seized all the beautiful aspects."

title: Yahtzee is still out there being mean about videogames, and good for him
text:
When the HMS Escapist sank everyone worth a damn swam away to form a YouTube channel called Second Wind , where Yahtzee Croshaw's video series Zero Punctuation continued under the name Fully Ramblomatic. It's not exactly the same—the people have glasses now—but it's continuing the essential work of being rude about videogames on the internet.
Back in the Before Times, when someone brought a videogame magazine to school we'd all gather round to flick through it, and the only measure of whether it was a good videogame magazine was if the captions on the screenshots were funny. I didn't notice until years later, but that meant we only read the British ones.
That particularly British tone is something Yahtzee's videos share. It might come across as flippant to some, but to me it's always read as deep care. Putting in the effort to make a description witty instead of plain means you're working harder to keep your audience engaged, and doing that for videogames suggests you care enough about them to want your audience to actually pay attention.
Yahtzee does that. Like Blackadder finding the 100th way to tell Baldrick he's an idiot, he never runs out of ways to complain about videogames. You know how Palworld made a big deal about letting you give your Fauxkémon guns? As Yahtzee points out, to actually do that in the game you have to "jump through so many hoops you feel like a spider in a bowl of Cheerios." That's a throwaway description I bet took the better part of the afternoon, and every episode is full of them.
When he actually likes something about a game it stands out. Not just because each tiny liferaft of positivity floats on the storm-tossed ocean of his negativity, but because his praise is as well-observed as his critique. When he says the turn-based combat of South Park: The Stick of Truth gives it a pacing that leaves natural gaps for jokes to fit in, that observation deepens your understanding of the game.
The internet's full of cynicism now, and I understand why people wouldn't be interested in more of it. But the videogame industry deserves to be disrespected every now and then, and videos that don't even bother to show a screenshot because contempt can be communicated just as well via stock images and a recurring catalogue of weird little guys are the kind of disrespect I can get behind.
I mean, he's wrong about Knights of the Old Republic , but I'll forgive him that one.

title: PvP pinball is such a good idea I can't believe I haven't played it before
text:
One of the great things about videogame conventions is there are always people up for playing a local multiplayer game, just waiting to be handed controls and thrown into a new experience. Which is how, at PAX Australia over the weekend, I found myself playing a game called Bumper Bout. It immediately impressed me with its concept, and then as I played a few rounds of it, with how it executed that concept.
Bumper Bout is two-player competitive pinball. If you know Puyo Puyo Tetris it's like that, but if you don't then imagine you're playing pinball on one half of the screen while someone else beside you is doing the same, only with the ability to flick balls across the divide. While you're trying to land a skill shot or just frantically deal with the balls already pinging between your flippers, the neighbor casually lobs another problem over the fence and says, "Deal with this. Good luck!"
Bumper Bout had the honor of being chosen as the final game of the Omegathon, the main stage tournament that plays out over the course of PAX, where it was introduced as a game made by someone who thought, "I love pinball, but no one ever dies."
Every time a ball goes down the ballhole you lose a heart, and the first player to lose five hearts loses the round. But scoring points by hitting bumpers and targets earns attack balls that you can zip over to harass your opponent, or store until you get four of them, unlocking your character's ultimate ability—which might let you create a gravity well or, if you're playing the pirate, throw bombs around the already hectic playfield.
Those playfields include a space level where satellites and moons bounce into each other to make even more chaos, and a foosball table where the flippers also activate half the player standees so you can use them to flick balls around as well. It takes a lot to overcome the noise and overwhelm of a busy show floor, but while I was playing Bumper Bout I was fully locked in.
I've seen plenty of demos that are popular at conventions fail to translate that popularity to the final release, but I hope that Bumper Bout can manage it. It's got singleplayer, with arcade and survival modes planned, and the final version will have online multiplayer too. You can try the demo for yourself on Steam , and the full game will be out on October 29.

title: Seamless Landing mod looks set to bring Starfield another step closer to No Man's Sky
text:
There are mods for Seamless Grav Jumps and for Seamless Planet Takeoffs . But when you arrive at a planet in Starfield you still have to choose a landing spot, and then watch a loading screen and an animation. It's another thing that contributes to the feeling your spaceship is more like a house that can teleport.
When you're in space, Starfield's planets are basically just textures you can fly right through if you put in the hours to try it, as Alanah Pearce discovered back when the RPG's boundaries were still being explored. It seemed like one gap modders would never be able to paper over, but Frederik Wessberg has apparently managed it.
The video of his work-in-progress mod shows a planetary approach, complete with heating effects on the ship during atmospheric entry, a moment of white as he hits a layer of clouds, and then the ship just lands. It seems like the clouds are there to mask a moment of loading, but Wessberg says "the cloud cover is in fact not a fancy loading screen."
He goes on to explain, "The clouds are not covering loading – they're helping make the seam as minimal as possible right at the point when we do the final cell switch, in terms of lighting and exposure, and terrain color. For airless moons and planets, I just do the switch with no veil, which is fine in that context as the lighting and exposure won't change as much between the two cells (although there I do some extra exposure matching). The underlying loading mechanism is entirely done in the background, while the game is still interactive. We just wait until the assets are finished loading in, and then we do the swap."
To make that work, the floating textures had to be replaced with actual models of the planets and moons. "I had to completely reimplement Starfield's planet rendering in space in 3D," Wessberg says, "in a way that looks detailed and sharp at every altitude.
"Thankfully, Starfield is actually amazingly physically accurate, and in many ways a true space simulator – it just doesn't ever reveal this to the player, but I could leverage it in my design here. So, the planet rendering is based upon Starfield's biome data and exact surface maps, including climate data, atmospheric composition data, and takes into account things like orbital phase, distance to the sun, distance to the moon(s) orbiting the planet and how they contribute moonlight, and so on. The philosophy is: Starfield's data is the 'truth', but we then modulate it by real physics."
The finished version of the mod, which will be freely available on Nexus Mods, will let players fly manually in low orbit, or turn on the autopilot and walk around the ship as you descend from orbit, and land anywhere you like—even on water. There's a post on Wessberg's Patreon with the details.

title: Star Wars Galactic Racer's devs tested its roguelite progression system by turning it into a board game
text:
Years ago, I read that Jake Solomon prototyped the Firaxis reboot of XCOM by making a simple board game version. Something rudimentary that could be played in the office on scrap paper to get ideas across and figure out where the fun would be, without having to commit. But it's surprising to hear the same idea being used for a game as different from XCOM's turn-based tactics as Star Wars Galactic Racer.
As Fuse Games' creative director Kieran Crimmins told Eurogamer , "You can't know if you can feel the system until you can play the system." And so the early prototype of this high-speed arcade racing game was indeed a board game.
"You know, modern engines are so capable that you can do a lot of it in-software," CEO Matt Webster said, "but there's still something [about that which is] not as fast as getting a written idea down. From a board game perspective, you sort of decouple yourself from a particular prototype and you're talking about moment-to-moment."
Specifically, the board game simulated Galactic Racer's progression system. Its rewards differ based on the event, but typically offer tuning points to spend on one of three random stats, and maybe a part for your speeder that will affect its abilities or grant a bonus related to a specific status effect. After several races you get to go shopping, and spend the credits you've earned on more upgrades and parts, or a whole new ability.
It's a progression system right out of a roguelite, with new unlocks added to a pool so they might appear in future runs, and each run handing out tuning points that can be used for permanent upgrades that carry over between them. Not something you expect in a racing game, and a system that presumably needed a bit of road testing to find the fun.
"There's a prototyping tool for every kind of system that you want to prototype," Crimmins said, "and the one that you pick should be the one that gets you there the quickest, and gets you to validate the emotion the quickest. So when it came to upgrades and meta progression, I can do a board game in a day. I mean, I say 'board game'. A lot of it is Post-its and a scribble and some dice. But we're trying to validate those feelings as quickly as possible. So you just pick the best tool for the moment."

title: Steam Week in Review: The curious case of Wonder Boy in Monster Land's dubious PC debut
text:
Wonder Boy in Monster Land released in Japanese arcades in 1987 and for the Sega Master System the following year. Its success led to numerous ports, including to ZX Spectrum, Commodore 64 and Atari ST. Oddly, it never received an official PC port, though that long absence appeared to have come to an end on September 28.
Did fans rejoice? Not really.
The Steam listing for Wonderboy in Monster Land raises one immediate red flag: note the rookie error of "Wonderboy" versus Wonder Boy. The developer and publisher is Retro Maniac, whose only other Steam game is Street Hoop, or Street Slam, an old Data East arcade game from 1994.
To bring you up to speed: LAT Corp owns all IP and assets once belonging to Westone Bit Entertainment, the creators of the original Wonder Boy games. But at the same time Sega, confusingly, owns the Wonder Boy trademark. In other words: LAT Corp owns the games, Sega owns the name. Both parties would need to OK any Wonder Boy re-release bearing the Wonder Boy name.
Box art for Wonder Boy in Monster Land on Master System (Image credit: Sega) While the "Wonderboy" misspelling is damning, a Wonder Boy game appearing on Steam without SEGA or LAT Corp prominently displayed isn't unusual. Wonder Boy Returns Remix, which is a "remake" of the original Wonder Boy, lists CFK Co., Ltd as developer and publisher. Not only was it officially licensed, but series creator Ryuichi Nishizawa was involved. Meanwhile, Wonder Boy: The Dragon's Trap is a thorough remake of the 1989 Master System original, developed by Lizardcube and published by Dotemu. It's also officially licensed. Each listing discloses as much in the Steam page fine print which appears under system requirements.
There's also the wider confusion around the name Wonder Boy itself, which reared its head with the release of Monster Boy and the Cursed Kingdom in 2019. Since rights to Wonder Boy games are split between LAT Corp and Sega it's necessary to get an OK from both to publish a Wonder Boy game with a Wonder Boy name. But what if you can only get the blessing of one? This dynamic was in play with Monster Boy, which is definitely, spiritually a Wonder Boy game—it had Nishizawa's handprints all over it—though publisher FDG Entertainment didn't license the Wonder Boy name from Sega, hence the name.
To confuse matters even more, the original arcade version of Wonder Boy released as Adventure Island in the United States, spawning a parallel line of unrelated follow-ups.
So what is a Wonder Boy game, then? Very few but diehards know off the top of their head, and if this new arcade "port" is illegitimate, it's probably released with full knowledge that this confusion will help it fly under the radar.
I wouldn't have thought twice about it if it weren't for the Wonder Boy Universe fan account on X, which raised the alarm on September 28. Composer on the original game, Shinichi Sakamoto, also weighed in , agreeing that the Retro Maniac port is illegitimate while pointing out that it's not available in Japan. (Sakamoto also claims it's been downloaded 10,000 times on Steam, though I don't know where he got that figure).
It turned out to be a problem that affected me directly. Apparently, it has already been downloaded 10,000 times on Steam. Yet, when accessing Steam from Japan, it doesn't show up—instead, you get a message saying, "This item is currently unavailable in your region."I am currently in the process of requesting its removal. September 29, 2026
Against my better judgement I bought and downloaded the alleged illegitimate version of Wonderboy in Monster Land, and can confirm it's simply a ROM running in the MAME arcade emulator (I've since requested a refund, which was issued promptly). The one obvious change is that a splash screen bearing the Sega logo has been removed.
The splash screen for the Retro Maniac version
The splash screen as depicted by YouTube channel Retro Fighters, playing an arcade ROM
(There's another variation depicted here , only Monster Land is in English rather than Japanese. The SEGA logo remains).
I reached out to Valve about the listing but didn't hear back. I also reached out to Sega several times but received no response. The Wonder Boy Universe X account claims the Retro Maniacs listing is "in the process of being DMCA'd by officials". Presumably they have a direct line to Sega or LAT that I don't have, because only Sega or LAT can file a DMCA. According to Valve's own documentation a DMCA complaint is processed in a maximum of 72 hours but can take longer if the situation is more complex.
Complex or not, Valve's documentation also shows what happens if your listing has a DMCA filed against it. Importantly, a public-facing notice will appear on the Steam page reading "A DMCA takedown notice has been filed on this item". That is yet to happen with Retro Maniac's listing.
This kind of thing happens a lot on mobile storefronts, especially for abandonware. But Wonder Boy in Monster Land isn't, at least strictly speaking, abandonware. I can't say I'm especially worried for Sega or LAT: it's obviously legally wrong for Retro Maniac to upload and profit from a game it didn't make or license—assuming that is the case—but Sega and LAT do themselves no favours by not having legitimate versions of Wonder Boy games easily available on Steam. Monster Lair and Monster World (but not Monster Land) used to be available as part of the SEGA Mega Drive and Genesis Classics collection, but that was removed from Steam in 2024.
Still, it's pretty funny how easily one can simply upload a rip off Wonder Boy game on Steam in 2026. A fortnight after its initial launch, Wonderboy in Monster Land is still officially available, and enthusiasts continue to wonder whether they should support it or not.

Who needs parks, places to live, shops etcetera, when the land they inhabit would be better served by a car park? That's the dystopian premise of Car Park Capital, which has you destroying the world with vast stretches of yellow-lined tarmac. In addition to turning the world an ashy shade of grey, you'll also need to convince people that they like it. Sounds familiar.

Silver Pines is a sidescrolling, rotoscoped horror with the structure of a metroidvania. You're a PI sent to a rundown small town to find missing rock musician Eddie Velvet. "A game about nostalgia, escapism and what lurks inside 'dead' physical media," reads the Steam description. It has some arrestingly bizarre pixel art.

title: Shogun 2 deserved better
text:
I blink and I've somehow spent another 30 hours in Shogun 2. Undoubtedly my favorite of the older Total War games—and I don't say that lightly as someone who also has big hour counts in Rome and Medieval 2—there's just something so straightforward about the second Shogun; an elegant simplicity complimented by a period where the Creative Assembly was clearly having fun experimenting with all sorts of ideas.
It's no wonder it chose to remaster the game despite the fact it's arguably the best aged Total War there is. I'd happily go back and play Shogun 2 over Rome 2, or even Attila, which I think speaks to how well it holds up. It's definitely nice to play Shogun 2 with improved visuals (if you like the new style), modern unit controls, and full Japanese voice acting, but I think Creative Assembly missed the mark in terms of the remaster's other additions.
To give it a fair shot, I started with one of the newly introduced island-bound minor factions, Honma. I always love conquering this island in campaigns because they have a gold mine, plus starting on an island in the north adds loads of possibilities. The first thing I noticed, though, is that none of the 50 new minor factions in Shogun 2's campaigns get unique bonuses, which would've gone a long way to distinguishing them from the minor faction unlocker mods Shogun 2 already had.
(Image credit: Creative Assembly) Without any passive bonuses to define playstyle, or tweaks to every faction starting with the same units, location is the only differential for these clans. I also discovered that the trade system hasn't been updated to account for single-region island factions, meaning my beloved Honma was only able to trade with one faction for the entirety of the campaign. Again, a QoL tweak would have made sense there.
In terms of the additions you'll actually feel in your campaigns, the new "Realm Divide" difficulty options for the endgame, improved visuals and terrain, and reworked unit controls are really the standout features—I went back to the original Shogun 2 afterwards, and the battlefield visual differences are notable. But the bird's eye battle view? The region overlay? I didn't use either of these once. The diplomatic quick deal is another somewhat useless addition. You don't form alliances or trade agreements anywhere near often enough in Shogun 2 to necessitate quick deal (as with Total War: Warhammer's 100s of factions), but the feature also doesn't include "arrange marriage".
(Image credit: Creative Assembly) A way to easily find out which factions had spousal candidates is the one diplomatic QoL change I genuinely would've found useful. While I did enjoy my campaign as Honma, I kept running into new QoL problems the original had that the remaster could have solved. No ability to merge units, for example, which would've been great in a game as attritional as Shogun 2, where unit upkeep isn't affected by remaining soldiers. Perhaps a numerical indicator for units in your army, which would save you counting them each time?
Shogun 2 still plays well, but that's not contingent on this remaster
What about agents accompanying armies getting left behind in settlements or on ships? Or how enlisted generals always appear back at your capital? I could go on, but there are so many QoL improvements this remaster could have made to Shogun 2 without infringing on the identity of the game. Even wider issues like siege pathfinding, which can still be dreadful, or problems with enemy AI.
I had one battle in the remaster where the besieging enemy general ran up to my wall, and then sat there for 40 minutes as I fast forwarded (a known bug I never even experienced in the original game). Or how about fixing the overly defensive naval AI, which sees you having to cross the entire map every battle just to engage enemy ships. You can see a full list of bug fixes for Shogun 2 - Complete Edition and it's not particularly extensive considering players have had 15 years to document every busted element, and I haven't even mentioned multiplayer bugs like the desync issue.
Yes, Shogun 2 still plays well, and I absolutely recommend it to Total War or strategy fans, but that's not contingent on this remaster. All the things that were great before are still great, whether it's battling with samurai to become shogun, or unloading a line of rifle infantry and cannon into enemy armies in Fall of the Samurai. If anything, I believe Shogun 2's quality as a game deserved a better and more extensive reworking than it's been given.
At least Shogun 2's DLC factions, who are now free, like the Christian Otomo, religious rebel Ikko-Ikki, or cannon-toting Saga in Fall of the Samurai, are some of the spiciest campaigns if you've never played them, and a whole bunch of people will get to try them for the first time (if they missed when those were previously free).
Any reason to return to Shogun 2 in 2026 is something to be celebrated, but I just wish Complete Edition felt more extensive and essential versus leaving so much undone. If you own Shogun 2 already, you'll get a month-long 75% discount when the game launches on Steam on October 13, while owners of the original will get all the legacy faction DLC for free, as mentioned.

You're looking for the "Emissive" option (Image credit: Embark Studios) Key deets
💡 Arc Raiders now has an option to turn off the light on your backpack.
💡 This is the "Emissive" toggle in each backpack's cosmetic menu.
Arc Raiders has made lots of new tweaks and additions with Frozen Trail's 2.0 update, but one long-requested change of significant note is that you can turn off the light on your backpacks.
To do this, you need to:
Select the "Raider" menu.
Enter "Customization" on the bottom left of the screen.
Go to the "Style" menu at the top.
Choose "Backpack" on the left side.
Toggle the Emissive option to "off".
As you'll see, while looking at the backpack, the light will disappear and reappear as you toggle this, though where exactly the light is varies from pack to pack. This should help you be a little sneakier, though it might make your character a bit harder to spot in some of the game's darkest areas.

title: 'The algorithm continues to properly prioritise Mister Biddy Blas'—Star Wars: Galactic Racer has created the perfect creature
text:
Star Wars: Galactic Racer is out, and it's pretty solid, netting a firm 76 score in our Galactic Racer review . It's also, as should always be the case with Star Wars videogames, full of funny little guys. None so funny as Biddy Blas. Why is Biddy Blas so popular? Just listen to his voice actor having an absolute ball. I will have the words "SCRIB DOON" burned into my brain forevermore:
I'm not even really seeking out much Galactic Racer content, and this guy's been cropping up on my recommended feeds, as observed by Lucasfilm Games executive producer Craig Derrick on X : "The algorithm continues to properly prioritize Mister Biddy Blas. I love it."
Blas is, in essence, a perfect "Glup Shitto". A fake character used as a sort of symbolic memetic stand-in for obscure Star Wars background characters that somehow become people's favourites. Blas isn't the first crocin to make an appearance in Star Wars, however—that was in Solo: A Star Wars Story.
Which is a relatively recent addition for Glup status, and as such I can't tell you much about the Crocin, other than the fact they apparently need to wear those goggles to protect their sensitive eyes from harsh sunlight. Owing to the fact that, on their home planet, they live in big caverns.
For Biddy Blas, however, I can only imagine he needs them to avoid scalding his sclera from the shine of his glorious racing prowess-slash-approaching intergalactic fandom. Which he insists that he already has—hard-earned via a supposed stint as a Huttball player and jatz trumpeter (not to be confused with another music genre, jizz).
He's really just the perfect mixture of shrill-voiced, delusional, and hideous to make his way into all-timer Star Wars character fame. Where he belongs, because he is Biddy Blas. Remember the name.

title: Here come the weird and wonderful mods for the Steam Frame, as Valve drops the full CAD files for free
text:
Valve has released the CAD files for the Steam Frame , allowing modders the perfect opportunity to get to work on their own creations for the VR headset.
The light blocker—the bit that sits between the bridge of your nose and the headset—is primed for user replacement, as are the head strap, battery housing, facial interface and more. This CAD release includes the lot, along with the core module and controllers.
Valve has confirmed it is working on an upgraded head strap with interchangeable batteries and off-ear speakers for the Steam Frame. That's " coming soon ". With this CAD release, perhaps we'll see more options for third parties in future, too.
The docs also detail how to interface with the expansion port , or auxiliary port as Valve calls it. This sits just to the front of the user's nose and is a way for a user to add in powered accessories, ie the Arcturus Vision RGB camera—I've been playing around with that for a couple of weeks and it's a pretty wicked upgrade. With one Gen4 PCIe lane alongside power and camera functionality, all laid out in the docs, there's a bunch more that could be done with the port. I'm just hoping someone runs with it.
With this release, Valve has a full sweep of CAD files available for all of its most recent products. There's the Steam Deck , Steam Machine , Steam Controller , and now Steam Frame. That's how it should be done, people.

title: 'Your washing machine is subject to more safety rules than AI' says Microsoft president
text:
Microsoft president Brad Smith claims that AI is currently less regulated than the food we eat and the utilities we rely on. "Right now, your washing machine is subject to more safety rules than AI," Smith said, "Every carton of milk that you see in the grocery store is subject to safety rules and inspection."
Smith isn't just talking about the US either, calling for safety rules to be put in place globally. Smith called for various safety measures while speaking on the BBC's Big Boss podcast , including a legal obligation to notify victims if their systems have been compromised by rogue AI agents. This would definitely be timely, given how OpenAI's agents hacked into Hugging Face and were the source of various other ' incidents ' earlier this year.
Smith also advocated for "outside evaluators" to test AI products before release, and a "safety brake" for autonomous systems, describing AI as both a "tool and a weapon." These comments run counter to the sentiment of the US administration; President Trump's current strategy demonstrates little desire to pump the brakes, instead hoping to chart ' a decisive course to cement US dominance in artificial intelligence .'
Last month, the US president issued an executive order that renames 'Artificial Intelligence' to 'Super Intelligence .' Shortly before that, Trump Media partnered with AI search engine Perplexity to create Truth Search AI, in a bid to " end Big Tech's assault on free speech ." All of that is to say, Trump appears to still be all-in on AI .
Unsurprisingly, the Microsoft boss is looking to places beyond the US to lead the regulatory charge, saying, "Most people that I know would say, if you ask them, 'name the country that is the leader in having this technical capability,' they would say, 'it's very simple. It's the United Kingdom. They are the best.'"
(Image credit: Travelpix Ltd via Getty Images) The UK government established what is now known as the AI Security Institute back in 2023, apparently the first state-backed AI safety body of its kind. It's a weird thing to feel anything like national pride over, but this Brit will take it—alongside the reminder that we've seen about three different Prime Ministers enter 10 Downing Street since the institute was established such a relatively short time ago.
Anyway, as for the wider AI industry, it's not just Brad Smith advising caution. Back in September, an ex-Anthropic and OpenAI researcher made the attention grabbing claim that AI developments "could kill us all by the end of the decade ." Around the same time, Anthropic boss Dario Amodei made more measured calls for AI development to slow down .
Similarly to Smith's suggestions, Amodei also outlined the need for "embedded evaluators who have employee-like access to verify safety practices and report incidents." Since then, executives from Nvidia, Google, OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, and SpaceX all agreed to work with independent auditors as part of signing White House Accord on Super Intelligence . Brad Smith says Microsoft would be "happy to sign it," describing the Accord as "a good step."
However, Smith was also cautious about the document's emphasis on self-regulation. He said, "The good companies will do what you want. It's the companies that are not as responsible that you need to worry about."

title: The RTX 4090 launched four years ago today, and now the RTX 5090 is rumoured for the chop, I can't help but look upon it with a warm glow
text:
Join me in saying "Happy birthday" to the RTX 4090, Nvidia's enthusiast-level graphics card of the previous generation. It launched four years ago today, October 12, with an eye-watering MSRP of $1,499.
Well, eye-watering for the time. The cheapest RTX 5080 I can find right now is this Asus Prime variant for $1,640 , which is a sure sign of how things have changed in the past four years. When the second-from-top Nvidia card is now significantly more expensive than the launch MSRP of the previous generation big boi model, it's pretty easy to see how far we've fallen.
And the RTX 4090's direct replacement, the RTX 5090, has reached near-unobtanium status. We've stopped tracking it on our graphics card price watch page , as the only listings around are priced at ludicrous levels from third-party sellers we're not comfortable recommending. Now rumours suggest Nvidia may have halted production of RTX 5090 chips for the consumer market , with the GB202 silicon being used for data center and professional GPUs instead.
Which makes me think of the RTX 4090 with a heavy dose of nostalgia. I had a hunt through the PC Gamer kit cupboard recently and came across our review sample, an absolute cinderblock of a GPU that still looks outrageous today. And that's before you get to the specs sheet, which is still impressive in 2026.
24 GB of GDDR6X. 76.3 billion transistors. 16,384 CUDA cores, a 56% increase over the RTX 3090 . 128 shader modules, 128 ray tracing cores, 512 Tensor cores. This is still a giant of a graphics card even by modern standards, and I know quite a few gamers still running one. They bit the bullet and paid the then-exorbitant price tag, and have been enjoying the monstrous power of their over-specced GPU ever since.
(Image credit: Future) If you had the cash on hand at the time, buying one was, in hindsight, a pretty smart move. Our Dave quite rightly called out the prohibitive pricing in his RTX 4090 Founders Edition review , but couldn't help but be impressed by its gaming chops—and it also provided us our first proper look at DLSS Frame Generation, in its early 2x form.
With so much grunt on offer, in combination with a new framerate-assisting feature, those who could swallow the price tag ended up with a GPU that still kicks like the proverbial mule all these years later.
And now an RTX 5080 costs more cash, with lesser raw performance (although with Multi Frame Generation support, which seems to have split the room in terms of gamer opinion), dropping such a sum on Nvidia's halo card seems to have worked out well for those who could afford it.
The RTX 5090 , however, has always been a more controversial GPU. Launching with a $1,999 MSRP (and soaring well above that in the retailer listings almost from the off), it's always been more difficult to square in terms of the price/performance metric—even if it does outperform the RTX 4090 by a considerable amount.
(Image credit: Future) And again, Multi Frame Generation is still a point of contention for some. The RTX 5090 remains the poster boy for the tech, despite being announced alongside the RTX 5080, RTX 5070 Ti , and RTX 5070 at CES 2025. I remember covering the announcement alongside my colleagues in Las Vegas, and wondering how the PC gaming community would react.
Yes, it boosts the number of frames displayed considerably. But it was always going to further the "fake frames" debate that was already rumbling underneath the older, 2x frame gen implementation. And while the RTX 5090 is still a massively powerful GPU in its own right, the pricing was sure to push many gamers out in the cold. Particularly if they had an RTX 4090 in their rig already. Why upgrade, when your current card was still an absolute monster?
Perhaps that's the legacy of the RTX 4090. The more I think about it, the more I think it might be the last halo GPU that made sense for a regular consumer to buy. It danced with a concept we tend to avoid mentioning in this industry—futureproofing, a dirty word I use with extreme caution here.
(Image credit: Future) Certainly, graphics card pricing looks to be turbo-screwed for the foreseeable future. And while the RTX 60-series is likely to be a way out yet, I can only imagine that whatever RTX 6090-equivalent is coming our way will be both ludicrously priced, and stuffed full of Tensor cores for more Multi Frame Generation shenanigans, now with DLSS 5 thrown on top.
Neural rendering is the future , as far as Nvidia is concerned. More hardware doohickies to supplement it, with less focus on raw performance uplift? That's where my money would be going.
Something about the four year anniversary of Nvidia's now-legendary 40-series card makes me pine for the days when GPUs were more straightforward affairs, raw graphics-crunching monsters available for sums that were at least somewhat within reach for those of us with more modest salaries.
Which is a wild thing to say about a $1,499, four-year-old GPU, I know. But the state of graphics card pricing in 2026 has thrown all previous metrics for a loop, and there's not a whole lot we can do about it. Anyway, raise a glass to the RTX 4090 with me. Somehow, I have a feeling we won't see its like again.

title: I am the controller now: MIT engineers have created a 'second skin' that could one day track whole bodies in VR
text:
Remember when they did motion capture on a cube ? Well, more specifically, they put actor Jack Quaid in a motion capture suit and then they put him inside a cube for his role in God of War Laufey. As charming as that cutting edge cuboid is, I think VR gamers and Vtubers are gonna be all over fresh research out of MIT.
Engineers at MIT have developed a sheet full of optical fibres that can digitally reconstruct its own shape even as it is flexed and folded. According to MIT News , the team reckons their tech could be fashioned into a garment that could then be used to accurately mirror your real-world movements in a game.
Though currently a bulky prototype, the flexible sheet could one day be worn like a second skin that can more accurately track the transformation of a surface, rather than the movement of, say, fixed points on a traditional motion capture suit. What's arguably even cooler though is that the sheet is shown in a demo video to remain functional even as an engineer pierces it with a hole puncher . Basically, this tech stands a good chance of surviving any clumsiness experienced while in VR.
Light from the bendy optical fibres inside the sheet is tracked and then interpreted by a specially developed algorithm. As the sheet bends, so do the fibres, which also dictates how much light can pass through them. This kind of structure is known as a waveguide.
Qifan Yu is a mechanical engineering graduate student at MIT, and one of the co-authors of the paper based on this project . Yu explains, "People have used waveguides to sense the shape of a line, which they have applied to a robot arm to see how it curves, but they haven’t been applied to surface shape sensing, to reconstruct the 3D shape of a surface. That’s what we’re trying to do here."
(Image credit: Kilito Chan via Getty Images) According to Yu, the team's algorithm reconstructs the movement of the actual sheet with a margin of error that's "less than 0.4 centimeters." He adds, "Existing designs, which are based on rigid sensors, have errors of around 1 to 2 centimeters."
Besides potentially more detailed performance capture, this tech could be used to control in-game movements or even aid patients undergoing physical therapy. Yu says, "In physical therapy, you often need to gather patient data on how they are moving and stretching their arm during rehabilitation, for example. Surface shape sensing could be very useful in that way."
The team is planning to trim down the prototype. Currently, the optical fibres measure 1 millimetre thick but alternate fabrication methods could potentially make these fibres thinner than a human hair at mere tens of micrometres. Let's just say, no matter how dweeby it makes me look, I'm looking forward to donning a shape-sensing garment at some point in the future and jumping into VR with both feet.

title: Schrödinger's GPU set for an early 2027 release as the dead/alive 24 GB RTX 5080 Super box is shaken once more
text:
It kinda looks like the only actually gaming-focused Nvidia GPU we're going to be left with next year is an RTX 5070 Ti . And even then only at a massively inflated price point. That's my personal takeaway from the rumours of the RTX 5090 being axed in favour of shifting GB202 GPUs to professional RTX Pro cards, and of a 24 GB RTX 5080 being brought in to replace the 16 GB version in early 2027.
This comes from almost a throwaway paragraph towards the end of a post on Benchlife about the bye-bye of the RTX 5090 from commercial production. According to the Taiwanese outlet, add-in board/card partners (AIBs or AICs) have been informed, verbally, that while they don't have anything concrete as yet, a 24 GB RTX 5080 will have its "product development data" released soon.
So, folks such as Asus and MSI have reportedly not been told much about the proposed new card, and that I would therefore take to mean we are nowhere when it comes to actual production right now. But, given that 24 GB was the VRAM quotient for a previously proposed RTX 5080 Super , there's a good chance those partners already have pretty much all the info they need to be able to spin up production in good time for a Q1 2027 launch.
But these are still naught but rumours, and the RTX 50-series Super/refresh has been on and off again more times than a six month-old Windows 11 machine trying to finish an update. So, I would still not be able to guarantee we're going to see one silicon iota of a new GeForce GPU in 2027. That's despite leaky personality, Moore's Law is Dead, stating their sources claimed an RTX 6090 launch is due in the first half of next year .
But, after a fallow 2026, I could see a GPU refresh of this type landing around or just after CES in 2027. It's not a big release, or even a gaming-centric release, even if it's noted as a GeForce graphics card. That's because the GB203 chip inside the RTX 5080 is already being fully utilised, so any new card will not have any higher core counts, and therefore isn't going to deliver any real gaming improvements.
What will benefit from having 24 GB of fast VRAM are the local AI models well-heeled builders want to use. Those builders who don't want to fork out for the sorts of high-end professional cards all the GB202 GPUs are being funnelled towards. If this is the way of things, then those users will go for the 24 GB RTX 5080 where once they would have plucked the RTX 5090 from the shelves.
All future GB202 supplies are RTX Pro exclusive October 10, 2026
Benchlife seems to be suggesting that as well as the RTX 5090, the standard 16 GB RTX 5080 will be end-of-life'd, too. Which means the top two cards of the RTX Blackwell generation will be effectively tied off for gamers, leaving just the RTX 5070 Ti, with its $1,500 sticker price, as the top-end choice for us PC peeps.
Nvidia giveth and Nvidia taketh away. And then taketh away again, I guess.

title: People are being robbed of crypto by a tiny chip implanted in their hardware, with $100 million said to have been stolen already
text:
I never got into crypto, but when I was considering doing so I was pretty quickly convinced that I should use a hardware wallet to store my private keys, as these are usually considered to pose less of a risk of being hacked and stolen than storing everything online. But alas, it seems one of the most reputable hardware wallets on the market has fallen victim of a supply chain attack (via a reseller) that's reportedly left some users short of a tidy collective sum of at least $86 million and, according to YFarmX's calculations, potentially over $100 million .
Ledger, the hardware wallet maker in question, has since said that as part of its investigation into the reports of stolen crypto, it can indeed confirm that "one of the impacted users' devices contained an unauthorised hardware implant."
The company also says , "To date, all confirmed cases related to the disclosed draining incident of Oct 9th, 2026, involve devices sold through the Southeast Asia reseller CryptoBilis."
Ledger says CryptoBillis confirms it has ceased all sales of the wallet until the ongoing investigation is concluded. The company also says it is "working with the appropriate authorities to bring the bad actors to justice."
Judging from a disassembly of an affected device shared on Reddit , it looks like the battery was taken out to fit in the "unauthorised hardware implant." This implant, at least according to some reports , sat behind the screen where its padding should be. Importantly, the implant seems to be soldered and takes information from the screen, thereby avoiding the usual hardware tampering detection in the device.
72 hour update on reseller CryptoBilis incident 🔽As the investigation continues, we are working with relevant authorities. The volume of impacted devices is limited. We know this is concerning, especially for those directly affected, and we are reaching out to impacted users.To date, all confirmed cases related to the disclosed draining incident of Oct 9th, 2026, involve devices sold through the Southeast Asia reseller CryptoBilis. Our systems and direct sales channels remain unaffected. We take the CryptoBilis situation seriously and are actively investigating.We encourage impacted users to reach out to Ledger Support through official channels and file complaints with their local law enforcement authorities. As a reminder, CryptoBilis has confirmed having ceased all sales of hardware wallets.We are reminding our authorized resellers and distributors to source products only through authorized channels and never to restock returned products.Also, we strongly advise users not to purchase from unauthorized resellers, where the risk of buying suspicious, counterfeit or modified devices is important as nothing operates under ledger security guidelines.Security isn’t static and this incident underscores why we continuously review and strengthen our distribution and anti-tamper processes. We are continuously improving that work now and events like this strengthen our resolution: reviewing authorized reseller controls, advancing hardware protections, and cooperating with authorities. Thanks to @SEAL_911 for their collaborative support and all their efforts.This is an ongoing threat that doesn’t just impact Ledger, but the whole ecosystem, and we are calling others in the space to work with us on making improvements for users.We believe in jointly working with researchers, other vendors and partners on improving industry chain-of-custody practices and anti-tamper techniques. Raising the bar on physical supply-chain integrity benefits the entire ecosystem. If you have relevant information, contact security@ledger.com.For CryptoBilis buyers: do not initialize unused devices. If already set up, move to a new seed on a device from Ledger. If you have concerns that your device was impacted by the CryptoBilis incident, please contact Ledger Support through the official site: https://t.co/JUcWwJO9iF. Ledger Support is available 24/7 to answer your questions and concerns.Scammers often try to take advantage of incidents like this. Rely only on official Ledger channels. Ledger will never call you, DM you, or ask for your 24-word recovery phrase. October 11, 2026
The company does show disassembly images for its hardware wallets so you can take it apart and check everything looks how it should. But these implants are apparently easy to miss unless you're careful even with disassembly, and Ledger notes that its integrity checks "cannot detect unauthorized physical modifications to the hardware—such as spying implants—if the original Secure Element remains intact."
So, what is the safe way to look after your crypto? It seems the community isn't entirely certain itself , apart from keeping your keys entirely apart from tech, such as on 'paper' (preferably something more sturdier and durable, though).
(Image credit: Ledger) In this particular case, I would assume buying directly from Ledger might have mitigated the risk, too, though CryptoBillis was an official reseller. Anything to reduce that attack vector is a good idea, given increasing supply chain risks.
The Open Web Application Security Project (OWASP) said earlier this year that "software supply chain failures" are a big risk for web app security, and we've seen supply chains being targeted in other industries such as for home routers . It seems ordering from as close to the source as you can get to is extra-advisable, these days. I'd say that goes doubly so when you're dealing with storage for vast amounts of money, crypto or otherwise.

title: 马斯克加快AI智能体入口布局！旗下智能助手「Grok Bot」周活激增、冲至美国App Store效率免费榜Top8！
text:
七麦数据监测显示，10 月 11 日，马斯克旗下 X Corp 推出的 AI 智能助手应用「 Grok Bot 」升至美国 App Store 效率免费榜第 8。与传统的聊天机器人不同，「Grok Bot」是一款定位为“常驻型 AI 同事”的AI智能体产品，可全天候在线、能登录用户常用的各类应用程序和网站、像同事一样完成实际工作。另外据媒体报道，早在 9 月 14 日，其周活跃用户已达 41.8 万，较前一周激增 24%。
「Grok Bot」升至美国App Store效率免费榜第8
据七麦数据显示，「Grok Bot」于 2026 年 8 月 11 日正式上线 App Store，自上线以来，其榜单排名持续攀升并占据全球多市场效率免费榜 Top20。以美国市场为例， 10 月 11 日，该 App 在美国 App Store 效率免费榜冲至 Top8 ，截至 10 月 12 日 11 时，该 App 仍位列 Top9。
「Grok Bot」在美国 App Store 效率免费榜排名
据悉，用户可以在应用内快速搭建专注于不同任务的Bot，比如做市场调研、策划广告活动。这些Bot可以接入Gmail、Google Calendar、Notion、 Figma 、财务软件、AI编程助手等工作应用，在其中直接执行任务。Grok Bot可以"观察"用户操作，学会自主重复这些动作。Bot完成任务后会主动汇报，也可以设置为在发送邮件、付款或修改数据前先请求用户审批。
其产品功能还在持续迭代升级。 近日，据SpaceX官方发布公告显示，「Grok Bot」推出专属邮箱功能。 该专属邮箱能够协助用户注册各类在线服务、代为联络商家洽谈事务，以及自主安排日常日程，大幅提升了多步骤后台任务的处理效率。
「Grok Bot」给我们带来了哪些启示？
「Grok Bot」能在短期内快速攀升，既得益于在自家社交媒体的大力推广，也离不开产品本身在性能与任务执行能力等方面的差异化优势。从「Grok Bot」的 App Store 产品页面上可以观察到，「Grok Bot」 将产品核心卖点标注为能够自主完成实际工作的 AI 智能体。另据 x.ai 官网的发布公告介绍，「Grok Bot」自带独立云端运行环境，可以登录各类第三方工具、跨应用处理任务，遇到需要人为决策的环节，会主动请求用户确认。
对这类 AI 工作助手而言，产品页面和宣传素材首先要讲清楚具体的工作场景与可交付的使用价值，才能让用户找到下载理由。 因此分析这款产品的获客逻辑时，关键要思考：用户愿意为哪一类实际工作下载这款 App。其App Store 产品页面列举了邮件整理、发票归集、客户跟进等真实办公场景；官方使用指南进一步说明，手机与桌面可以访问同一台云端计算机。移动端的价值也由此多了一层：用户离开电脑后，仍可随时查看任务进度、补充资料，或处理需要本人确认的步骤。
面向这类需求，如果宣传素材只展示几句流畅对话，很难说服用户单独下载。同类团队，建议挑选一项产品已经稳定支持的任务，完整演示从下达指令到拿到最终结果的全流程，例如自动收集发票并整理清单，同时讲清楚需要授权哪些账户、哪些环节必须人工确认。广告素材和商店首屏展示的内容，需要能承接同一个宣传卖点。
另外，据 x.ai 官网在 8 月 26 日公告中披露，「Grok Bot」被纳入 SuperGrok 、Cursor Pro、Cursor Teams 等订阅计划内，订阅用户拥有独立使用额度。对于已经持有相关订阅权益的用户，尝试「Grok Bot」可以从既有权益出发；而对于第一次接触产品的新用户，则需要重新理解产品用途、账户规则和付费价值。两类人群面对的下载决策不同，但现有榜单无法区分这两类人群各占多少。
因此， 对于拥有多产品会员体系的 App，扩量前应先拆开两种用户来源——已有权益用户的激活与新增用户的获客，并分别进行统计和验证 ，而不能仅凭榜位表现来判断独立 App 的冷启动效果。普通独立团队则可以尝试优先验证新用户转化链路：用真实任务场景吸引用户，跟踪安装、账户授权、产出第一份可用结果，以及之后是否再次执行任务这一系列行为。
结语
「Grok Bot」上线以来的亮眼表现，印证了其不俗的市场潜力。普通团队可以借鉴的思路，是把产品能交付的工作结果讲清楚。如果点击、安装量上涨，但大量用户卡在账户授权或者首次任务环节，就要优先调整宣传素材预期、降低使用门槛说明；当新用户能够顺利完成任务、重复使用产品之后，我们可以再考虑加大该市场投放。后续这款产品是否还会有更加亮眼的表现，值得我们持续关注。
